title: Noninvasive comparison of cardiac output before and after mitral valve clipping using using HemoSphere® monitoring
summary:
When the mitral valve does not close properly (mitral regurgitation), blood leaks back into the left upper chamber of the heart with every heartbeat instead of being pumped fully into the body. To correct this, a procedure called mitral valve clipping is often performed, a catheter-based intervention in which a small clip is used to close the valve more tightly.
This study at University Hospital Bonn investigates how cardiac output, the amount of blood the heart pumps through the body per minute, changes immediately before and after this procedure. In addition, it examines how accurately a new, non-invasive measurement method (HemoSphere® system) performs compared with conventional invasive blood pressure measurement via an arterial catheter. The study aims to show whether the new method provides reliable values and could in future serve as a gentler alternative to conventional measurement. A total of 60 patients undergoing mitral valve clipping will be enrolled in the study.

interventions.name: Invasive haemodynamic monitoring using continuous, invasive arterial blood pressure measurement and non-invasive, continuous haemodynamic monitoring using the HemoSphere® system.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients undergoing mitral valve clipping. Use of arterial catheter and non-calibrated pulse wave analysis (HemoSphere)
Exclusion criteria:
No use of arterial catheters and non-calibrated pulse waveform analysis (HemoSphere)
